questions.question: Who discovered Sodium?
questions.solution: Sodium was first isolated in 1807 by Humphry Davy, who made it by the electrolysis of very dry molten sodium hydroxide, NaOH. Sodium is the sixth most abundant element on earth and comprises about 2.6% of the earth's crust.

questions.question: _________ is the process of restoring a forest that once existed but was removed at some point of time in the past.
questions.solution: Reforestation is the process of restoring existing forests and woodland that have been depleted, usually through deforestation. Reforestation can be used to rectify or improve the quality of human life by soaking up pollution.

questions.question: Who was the 2016 Men's Kabaddi World Cup Runner-Up?
questions.solution: The 2016 Men’s Kabaddi World Cup Runner-Up was Iran. The tournament was won by India, who defeated Iran 38-29 in the championship game to win their third Kabaddi World Cup.

questions.question: Which of the following won The Man Booker Prize 2016?

options.text: A Brief History of Seven Killings
The Narrow Road to the Deep North

questions.solution: The 2016 Man Booker Prize was awarded to Paul Beatty for her novel The Sellout. Beatty is the first US writer to win the Man Booker Prize.

questions.question: Jama Masjid of Delhi was built in which century?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Mughal emperor Shah Jahan** built the **Jama Masjid** between **1644 and 1656**.
 
• It was originally called **Masjid-i-Jahan-Numa**, meaning '**mosque commanding view of the world**'.

**Note**__:

**Century **is one plus the year is given, for example, if we talk about the year 2019 we say we are in 21st century (20+1) and if we talk about **1672 then it is 17th century (16+1).**

questions.question: Which base is present in milk of magnesia?
questions.solution:
• The base present in the milk of magnesia is Magnesium hydroxide.
 
• It is a white solid with low solubility in water and a common component of antacids.
 
• As an antacid, magnesium hydroxide works by simple neutralization, where the hydroxide ions combine with acidic H+ ions in the stomach to produce water.

questions.question: In the north-west, India shares its land boundaries with which country?
questions.solution: India shares its border with 7 countries of the world. In North West, India Shares its border with Pakistan. The length of our land border with Pakistan is roughly 3,220 km.

questions.question: Which amendment of the Constitution of India increased the age of retirement of High Court judges from 60 to 62 years?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **15th amendment**__ of 1963 rose the retirement age of High court judges from 60 to 62 and other minor amendments for rationalizing interpretation of rules regarding judges etc.
 
• __**Article 217**__ deals with the appointment of HC Judges.
 
• Supreme Court Judges retire upon attaining an age of __**65 years**__.
 
• __**Article 124 **__deals with the appointment of Judges of Supreme court.

questions.question: _________ means that the Supreme Court will reconsider the case and the legal issues involved in it.
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Appellate Jurisdiction**__.

__
 
• **Appellate jurisdiction**__ is the power of the apex court to review decisions and change outcomes of decisions of lower courts.
 
• The appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court can be invoked by a certificate granted by the High Court concerned under **Article 132(1), 133(1), or 134** of the Constitution.

questions.question: In humans, the sound is produced by the ________.
questions.solution: The larynx is usually called the voice box because it is where sound comes from. It is the one that manages the pitch and volume produced by mammals, and it is also the one that houses the vocal folds.

questions.question: The queen with the title Didda ruled over which part of India between 980 - 1003?
questions.solution: Didda was a daughter of Simharāja, the king of Lohara who ruled Kashmir from 958 CE to 1003 CE. She married the king of Kashmir, Ksemagupta, thus uniting the kingdom of Lohara with that of her husband.

questions.question: The vocal cords in men are about _______ long.
questions.solution: Men and women have different vocal fold sizes. The male vocal folds are about 20 mm in length while Female vocal folds are between 12.5 mm and 17.5 mm long. The difference in vocal fold size between men and women means that their voices have a different pitch.

questions.question: During their rule the British persuaded or forced cultivators in Madras to grow __________.
questions.solution: To increase their revenue the British decided that they could use Indian villages to grow crops like Rice, Wheat, Tea and Jute that were in demand in Britain. The forced the farmers to grow Jute in Bengal, Tea in Assam, Sugarcane in Uttar Pradesh, Wheat in Punjab, Cotton in Maharashtra & Punjab, and Rice in Madras.

questions.question: The __________ uses an addressing scheme known as URL to indicate the location of files on the web.
questions.solution: The World Wide Web is an information space where documents and other web resources are identified by Uniform Resource Locators, interlinked by hypertext links, and can be accessed via Internet. The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

questions.question: The part of the Himalayas lying between Satluj and Kali rivers is known as _________.
questions.solution: Kumaun Himalayas is the west-central section of the Himalayas in northern India, extending 200 miles from the Sutlej River east to the Kali River. It is bounded on the north by Tibet, on the east by Nepal, on the south by the state of Uttar Pradesh, and on the west by the Garhwal region.

questions.question: __________ says that if we keep increasing the employment of an input, with other inputs fixed, eventually a point will be reached after which the resulting addition to output (i.e., marginal product of that input) will start falling.
questions.solution: Law of diminishing marginal product states that while increasing one input and keeping other inputs at the same level may initially increase output, further increases in that input will have a limited effect, and eventually no effect or a negative effect, on output.

questions.question: The first formed primary xylem elements are called ___________.
questions.solution: Protoxylem is the part of the primary xylem that develops first, consisting of narrow, thin-walled cells. It matures much before the plant organ has completed their elongation and is smaller in diameter as compared to Metaxylem.

questions.question: Nereis, Pheretima (Earthworm) and Hirudinaria (blood sucking leech) are examples of which Phylum?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Nereis**,** Pheretima (Earthworm)** and** Hirudinaria** are examples of Annelida Phylum.
 
• The annelids are also known as the **ringed worms** and are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, coelomate, invertebrate organisms.
 
• **Other important features of Annelids are**

 
• They may be aquatic (marine and fresh water) or terrestrial; free-living, and sometimes parasitic.
 
• They exhibit organ-system level of body organisation and bilateral symmetry.
 
• They are triploblastic, metamerically segmented and coelomate animals.
 
• Their body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres and, hence, the phylum name Annelida

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Coelenterata**:

 
• They are aquatic, mostly marine, sessile or free-swimming, radially symmetrical animals
 
• The characteristic feature of this phylum is the presence of cnidoblasts or cnidocytes (which contain the stinging capsules or nematocysts) present on the tentacles and the body.
 
• Cnidoblasts are used for anchorage, defence, and for capture of prey. Eg.** Physalia** (Portuguese man-of-war), **Adamsia** (Sea anemone),** Pennatula** (Sea-pen), **Gorgonia** (Sea-fan), and **Meandrina** (Brain coral)

**Aschelminthes:**

 
• The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section, hence, the name **roundworms**
 
• They may be freeliving, aquatic and terrestrial or parasitic in plants and animals.
 
• Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
 
• They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and pseudocoelomate animals.
 
• Examples : **Ascaris** (Roundworm), **Wuchereria **(Filaria worm), **Ancylostoma** (Hookworm).

questions.question: Potato, tomato and brinjal are three different species but all belong to which genus?
questions.solution: Solanum is a diverse genus of flowering plants, which include two food crops of high economic importance, the potato and the tomato. It also contains the nightshades and horse nettles, as well as numerous plants cultivated for their ornamental flowers and fruit.

questions.question: In a centrally planned economy, the ________ plans all the important activities in the economy.
questions.solution: A centrally planned economy is an economic system in which government makes economic decisions rather than the interaction between consumers and businesses. The government of a centrally planned economy decides where and when production and investment will be directed.

questions.question: Most liquids that conduct electricity are solutions of acids, bases and ______.
questions.solution: Most liquids that are solutions of Acids, Bases and Salts conduct electricity. They conduct electricity due to the presence of Charged ions.

questions.question:
Which of the statements given below are correct?

1. The author of the novel 'Gilead' is Don Winslow.

2. The author of the novel 'Wolf Hall' is Stephen Dobyns.

3. The author of the novel 'To Kill a Mockingbird' is Harper Lee.
questions.solution: The author of the novel 'Gilead' is Marilynne Robinson while the author of the novel 'Wolf Hall' is Hilary Mantel.

questions.question: What was United Kingdom's rank in 2016 Human Development Index published by the United Nations Development Programme?
questions.solution: United Kingdom was placed at the 16th position in the 2016 Human Development Index. The index was topped by Norway while India’s rank was 131. The Human Development Index is a composite statistic of life expectancy, education, and income per capita indicators.

questions.question: Which railway station is used for immigration and customs of passengers who travel on the Thar Express between Pakistan and India?
questions.solution:
• Zero Point Railway station is used for immigration and customs of passengers who travel on the Thar Express between Pakistan and India.
 
• It is situated 8 km east of Khokhrapar, Sindh and lies on the Pakistan–India border.

questions.question: ________ scheme launched by the Central Government to eliminate open defecation by constructing toilets for households, communities.

options.text: Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan

questions.solution: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan aims to eliminate open defecation by constructing toilets for households, communities. The campaign was officially launched on 2 October 2014 at Rajghat, New Delhi by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
